hints: Focus on what happens when a Group 2 nitrate is heated, think oxide solid plus nitrogen dioxide plus oxygen.
Start by finding the moles of $\text{Mg(NO}_3)_2$ in 7.4 g using its $M_r$ of about 148.3.
Use the balanced equation ratio of nitrate to $\text{NO}_2$ to convert your moles into mass with $m = n \times M_r$.
walkthrough:
**Identify gas X and write the equation**

Group 2 nitrates always decompose the same way to metal oxide, nitrogen dioxide and oxygen. So X is $\text{NO}_2$.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$2\text{Mg(NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{MgO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$$

**Calculate moles of magnesium nitrate heated**

First find $M_r$ of $\text{Mg(NO}_3)_2$. Then use moles equals mass divided by $M_r$.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$M_r = 24.3 + 2 \times (14.0 + 3 \times 16.0) = 148.3$$
$$n(\text{Mg(NO}_3)_2) = \frac{7.4}{148.3} = 0.05 \text{ mol}$$

**Use the mole ratio to find mass of X**

From the equation, 2 mol nitrate gives 4 mol $\text{NO}_2$, so the ratio is 1:2. Multiply moles by $M_r$ of $\text{NO}_2$ (46.0) to get mass.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$n(\text{NO}_2) = 0.05 \times 2 = 0.10 \text{ mol}$$
$$m(\text{NO}_2) = 0.10 \times 46.0 = 4.6 \text{ g}$$

options.A: Not correct. 1.5 g is what you get if you mistake X for $\text{NO}$ ($M_r = 30$) with a 1:1 ratio ($0.05 \times 30$). The brown gas from nitrate decomposition is $\text{NO}_2$, not $\text{NO}$.
options.B: Not correct. 2.3 g comes from using a 1:1 mole ratio ($0.05$ mol $\times$ 46.0). Check the balanced equation, each $\text{Mg(NO}_3)_2$ contains two nitrate groups, so you get 2 mol of $\text{NO}_2$ per mol of reactant.
options.C: Not correct. 3.0 g comes from getting the 1:2 ratio right ($0.10$ mol) but using the wrong gas $\text{NO}$ ($0.10 \times 30$). Remember the oxide of nitrogen here is nitrogen dioxide, $\text{NO}_2$.
options.D: Correct. Well done. With $0.05$ mol of $\text{Mg(NO}_3)_2$ and a 1:2 ratio, you make $0.10$ mol of $\text{NO}_2$, which has mass $0.10 \times 46.0 = 4.6$ g.
